title: Design System: Hozaifa Bin Masud — Portfolio

display.purpose: The name in the hero README and the product name on a case study.

headline.purpose: Section headings and a case study's closing heading.

lead.purpose: The single positioning line under the display (a case study's tagline), about 32ch.

title.purpose: Project and role titles; case-study commit messages (20px, 24px from sm); the open directory row's title stays at 20px.

control.purpose: Button labels (500), field text (400), stack and fact values, filter chip labels, the directory's built-for column.

label.purpose: Form labels, section more-links, social links.

code.purpose: Nav links, dates and durations, emails, contact handles, stack keys, breadcrumbs, commit stat lines, the viewer counter, the directory's stack key, live count and more toggle, the about inventory's and the resume's skill keys.

code-ui.purpose: File names in explorers and tab strips; the case-study fact line; the directory's slugs, status lines, opens column and status summary.

code-label.purpose: Status bar, tags, file tabs, data keys, the directory's column header and chip counts, the resume's contact keys.

focus.name: field-focus
focus.purpose: Input and textarea focus (a 1px ring, not a shadow); danger when aria-invalid.

focus.name: selection
focus.value: background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--color-primary) 38%, transparent); color: var(--color-strong)

motion.name: ease-out-expo
motion.value: cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1)
motion.purpose: The default easing curve for transitions and entrances; everything but the hero lid.

motion.name: ease-out-quart
motion.value: cubic-bezier(0.25, 1, 0.5, 1)
motion.purpose: The hero lid's curve only (animate-assemble), so the swing is seen rather than spent at once.

motion.name: state-colour
motion.value: 200ms ease-out-expo
motion.purpose: Colour, background and border changes on hover, focus and selection.

motion.name: micro-transform
motion.value: 300ms ease-out-expo
motion.purpose: Arrow nudges (2px), nav underline scale, logo 90deg rotation, header border, mobile menu fade-and-drop (8px). Project explorer selection highlight gliding between files. The projects directory's chevron turning 180deg as a row opens.

motion.name: nav-indicator
motion.value: transform translateX + width (and opacity), 300ms ease-out-expo; transition none on resize
motion.purpose: One 1px orchid underline in the header glides to the current item, measured from the nav; it replaces the per-link scale-in underlines.

motion.name: assemble
motion.value: animate-assemble: assemble 1000ms cubic-bezier(0.25, 1, 0.5, 1) both (opacity 0 -> 1 by 25%; transform perspective(1600px) rotateX(16deg) translateY(28px) -> none; transform-origin bottom)
motion.purpose: The hero lid: the workspace window opens once on load like a screen lid hinged at its foot. The one authored moment.

motion.name: rise
motion.value: rise 520ms ease-out-expo both (opacity 0 -> 1, translateY 8px -> 0)
motion.purpose: The workspace window's contents (explorer rows and README content), staggered 140-460ms, rising inside the window as it opens. Also the contact form's status line, each new outcome rising inside the stable live region, and the /contact receipt's rows (delays 160ms + 60ms each, the sent row at 340ms).

motion.name: wipe
motion.value: wipe 420ms ease-out-expo both (clip-path inset(0 100% 0 0) -> inset(0), opacity 0.4 -> 1)
motion.purpose: Replays on the project preview pane each time a project file is selected. Field error messages wipe in, keyed on the message. On the contact page it brings in the sent receipt in place of the form, and brings the form back after "Write another" (only then, never on first paint).

motion.name: screen-next
motion.value: animate-screen-next: screen-next 420ms ease-out-expo both (opacity 0 -> 1, translateX 48px -> 0)
motion.purpose: Screen Viewer step forward: the next screen slides in from the right. Replaces the old wipe on the viewer image. Skipped under reduced motion.

motion.name: screen-prev
motion.value: animate-screen-prev: screen-prev 420ms ease-out-expo both (opacity 0 -> 1, translateX -48px -> 0)
motion.purpose: Screen Viewer step back: the previous screen slides in from the left.

motion.name: acknowledge
motion.value: animate-acknowledge: acknowledge 200ms ease-out-expo both (opacity 0 -> 1, scale 0.6 -> 1)
motion.purpose: A done action's mark pops into place: the copy-email button's String Green check.

motion.name: sending
motion.value: animate-sending: sending 1100ms cubic-bezier(0.65, 0, 0.35, 1) infinite (translateX -100% -> 250%), a 40%-wide 2px bar in Cursor White at 70%
motion.purpose: Sweeps along the primary Send message button's foot while the contact form is pending; mounted only while pending, hidden under reduced motion. The "Sending…" label carries the state.

motion.name: turn
motion.value: animate-turn: turn 640ms ease-out-expo both (opacity 0.35 -> 1; transform perspective(1000px) rotateY(-18deg) translateX(-16px) -> none; transform-origin left)
motion.purpose: A chosen project screenshot (or its empty frame) turns to face the reader: with the preview pane's wipe on the homepage, and in the projects directory each time a row opens (only inside a non-inert region).

motion.name: pointer-tilt
motion.value: TiltSurface: perspective(<depth>px) rotateX/rotateY up to <max>deg at the edge; each frame closes 12% on the pointer; eases to none on leave; will-change only while moving
motion.purpose: Mouse only, gated by (hover: hover) and (pointer: fine) and (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference); the outer box stays still and an inner plane turns. Hero window 3deg at 2000px; project screenshots 6deg at 1100px (homepage explorer and projects directory); training certificates 5deg at 1100px; case-study HEAD frame 2.5deg at 2400px.

motion.name: parallax
motion.value: data-depth="<px>": translate up to that many px with the pointer, inside a TiltSurface
motion.purpose: README content 14px and the explorer list 6px in the hero window; they drift inside their panes, which never separate.

motion.name: deck-peek
motion.value: three.js deck at rest: 3 cards behind the chosen screenshot, top edges peeking 9px each, 70 world px of depth apart; strength toward --color-bg-main in sRGB 0.45 / 0.315 / 0.18 by slot; 1 CSS px Hairline edge
motion.purpose: The project deck in the homepage explorer, from md: the one element that holds depth at rest. Flat unlit ShaderMaterial panes; canvas reaches 44px above the screenshot.

motion.name: deck-fan
motion.value: peek 9 -> 14px, depth 70 -> 120 per slot, rotateX -0.035 rad per slot; parallax -10px x and +6px y per slot from the TiltSurface eased pointer; each frame closes 14%
motion.purpose: A mouse over the screenshot fans the deck ((hover: hover) and (pointer: fine)); it also fans briefly while a selection glides. Off under reduced motion.

motion.name: deck-glide
motion.value: slot position eased 14% per frame toward the new slot; a card leaving the front for the far end jumps there behind the screenshot; first placement lands without motion
motion.purpose: Choosing a project moves the cards between slots so the change is seen. Under reduced motion the cards land at once and the deck stands static.

motion.name: shared-morph
motion.value: ::view-transition-group(.morph) 520ms ease-out-expo; image pair blurs 4px at 35%
motion.purpose: The project screenshot morphs between the homepage explorer or the projects directory and its case study (React ViewTransition share="morph", name project-shot-<slug>).

motion.name: tech-morph
motion.value: ::view-transition-group(.tech-morph) 520ms ease-out-expo
motion.purpose: On nav-forward only, a homepage stack technology's logo and name morph into the projects directory chip's (name tech-<slug>); the chip carries the name only while its filter equals the arriving ?stack.

motion.name: tab-edge
motion.value: ::view-transition-group(.tab-edge) 300ms ease-out-expo (name learning-tab-edge)
motion.purpose: The open tab's 1px orchid top edge slides between education.md and trainings.md as the page changes; an edge, so the named layer never covers text.

motion.name: page-turn
motion.value: perspective(2600px) translateX(+/-48px) rotateY(+/-7deg) -> none, pivoting on the edge the page leaves by; old: fade out 160ms ease-in + swing 460ms; new: fade in 240ms after 140ms + swing 520ms ease-out-expo (mirrored for nav-back)
motion.purpose: Directional page transitions for links with transitionTypes nav-forward / nav-back, turning like tabs on a carousel; the site header is pinned, the root does not animate and the screenshot morph is unchanged.

motion.name: dock
motion.value: translate + opacity 500ms ease-out-expo
motion.purpose: The docked status bar sliding up from, and back into, the foot of the screen.

motion.name: reading-progress
motion.value: scaleX 0 -> 1 linear, animation-timeline: scroll(root block)
motion.purpose: The 1px orchid reading line on the docked status bar; hidden without scroll-timeline support.

motion.name: rail-fill
motion.value: .rail-fill::after: Strong Hairline, scaleY 0 -> 1 from the top, linear, animation-timeline: --rail (view-timeline on the rail), animation-range: cover 50vh cover calc(100% - 50vh)
motion.purpose: The work log, learning log and case-study rails brighten from Hairline to Strong Hairline from each node down to the next as that stretch crosses mid-viewport. @supports (animation-timeline: view()) gated; stays under reduced motion.

motion.name: node-lit
motion.value: .node-lit: 1px ring Hairline -> Syntax Orchid -> Hairline, linear, animation-timeline: view(), lit across the reading band 50px either side of the middle line
motion.purpose: A plain node on the work log and learning log lights orchid while it is the commit being read, and returns to Hairline once passed; status nodes keep their colours and the case study's nodes keep their JS active state. Stays under reduced motion.

motion.name: scroll-wipe
motion.value: wipe keyframes, linear, animation-timeline: view(), animation-range: entry 5% entry 95%
motion.purpose: Each case-study screen wipes in from the left (clip-path, opacity 0.4 -> 1) as it scrolls into view, together with its stand; only with view-timeline support and prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference, otherwise the screen is simply shown.

motion.name: scroll-stand
motion.value: stand-up keyframes, linear, animation-timeline: view(), animation-range: entry 0px entry 360px (perspective(1400px) rotateX(-16deg) scale(0.97) -> none; transform-origin top)
motion.purpose: Case-study screens stand up to face the reader as they scroll in; inside @supports (animation-timeline: view()) and prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference.

motion.name: depth-settle
motion.value: depth-in: depth-settle keyframes, linear, animation-timeline: view(), animation-range: entry 0px entry 280px (perspective(1400px) rotateX(-7deg) translateY(36px) -> none; transform-origin top)
motion.purpose: Blocks settle from a slight lean as they scroll in: homepage sections after the hero, work-history roles, the about page's two sections, resume appendix sections and the contact channel list. Only transforms move; a block on screen at load rests flat. Railed logs are excluded. Same @supports and reduced-motion gate.

motion.name: node-lighting
motion.value: background and ring colour, 300ms ease-out-expo
motion.purpose: The case-study commit crossing the reading band (IntersectionObserver, rootMargin -45% 0px -50% 0px) lights its node Syntax Orchid; HEAD stays green.

motion.name: viewer-fade
motion.value: opacity 0 -> 1, 300ms ease-out-expo, transition-behavior: allow-discrete with @starting-style
motion.purpose: The Screen Viewer dialog fading in on open and out on close; its backdrop fades with the grow and shrink (see viewer-grow, viewer-shrink).

motion.name: viewer-grow
motion.value: WAAPI FLIP on the stage: transform translate + scale from the thumbnail -> none, 520ms cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1); ::backdrop opacity 0 -> 1 over 520ms ease-out-expo; controls and caption opacity 0 -> 1 in 200ms ease-out-expo after 240ms (@starting-style), at once under reduced motion
motion.purpose: A screen grows out of its thumbnail as the viewer opens, the contained image exactly over the thumbnail; a layer from the thumbnail's loaded file (its sizes) stands in while the full size loads. Skipped under reduced motion.

motion.name: viewer-shrink
motion.value: WAAPI on the stage: none -> thumbnail transform, 300ms cubic-bezier(0.7, 0, 0.84, 0), fill forwards; ::backdrop opacity -> 0 over 300ms; controls and caption opacity -> 0 in 200ms ease-out-expo
motion.purpose: Escape, the close button or a backdrop click shrink the screen back into its thumbnail (only when the thumbnail is in view), then the dialog closes and focus returns to the thumbnail. Skipped under reduced motion.

motion.name: row-open
motion.value: grid-template-rows 0fr -> 1fr, 300ms ease-out-expo; chevron rotate(180deg) 300ms ease-out-expo; row fill and orchid edge 200ms ease-out-expo
motion.purpose: A projects directory row opening in place to its panel and closing again; the closed panel is inert.

motion.name: dir-row-out
motion.value: ::view-transition-old(.dir-row-out) 120ms linear both (opacity -> 0, translateX -> -8px)
motion.purpose: Projects directory filter: rows that leave are gone first.

motion.name: dir-row-move
motion.value: ::view-transition-group(.dir-row-move) 300ms ease-out-expo, delay 80ms; old/new faces 100ms, delay 80ms
motion.purpose: Rows that stay hold, then glide to their new places, swapping old and new faces quickly; the Hiring Close below glides with them. Keyed <ViewTransition> rows, state change in startTransition.

motion.name: dir-row-in
motion.value: ::view-transition-new(.dir-row-in) 280ms ease-out-expo, delay 200ms (opacity 0 -> 1, translateY 10px -> 0)
motion.purpose: New rows rise in last. About 500ms in all, with no double exposure.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.value: animation and transition durations 0.01ms; view-transition animations 0s; smooth scroll off; the case-study scroll wipe and stand and the block settle are not applied; pointer tilt does not run; the project deck stands static, with no fan or glide; the screen viewer skips its grow, shrink and slides; the sending light is hidden
motion.purpose: prefers-reduced-motion: reduce collapses all motion (the reading line, the rail fill and the lit nodes still track the scroll).

narrative.overview:
The site is a One Dark code editor opened on Hozaifa's real work, in a professional register. The editor is carried by structure, not ornament: a window with a title bar, an explorer that doubles as navigation, tab strips, a status bar, file names that label sections, and a git-log timeline. Inside that chrome the writing is set like a well-made product page, in a humanist sans, so a recruiter or client reads prose while the developer's world stays visible at the edges.

Surfaces are three flat One Dark layers separated by 1px hairlines with square corners. Colour comes from syntax roles: orchid acts and marks focus or the current file, green means live or available, amber means in progress, red means error, blue underlines outbound links. Everything else is cool charcoal and gray. Density is calm: generous section rhythm, compact chrome, reading columns held to about 65 characters.

Motion is brief and carries continuity rather than decoration, and it is where the workspace gets its depth: the panes stay flat, while the window and the media in it turn in perspective and ease back to flat; the one thing that holds depth at rest is the project deck, where the next projects stand back behind the chosen screenshot. On load the workspace window opens once like a screen lid hinged at its foot, its contents rising in a stagger as it swings up. With a mouse the window, the project screenshots and the certificates lean toward the pointer, and inside the window the README and the explorer list drift by a few pixels within their panes. In the project explorer the selection highlight glides to the chosen file, the preview pane wipes in from the left and its screenshot turns to face the reader from its left edge, while behind it the deck fans under the mouse and its cards glide between places as the choice changes. Opening a case study from the homepage explorer or the projects directory morphs the project screenshot into its place on the new page while the rest of the page turns away like a tab on a carousel, and the breadcrumb back reverses it; a stack technology opens the directory filtered on it, its logo and name morphing into the chip. In the projects directory a row opens in place, growing to its content while its chevron turns and its screenshot turns to face the reader, and a filter moves the list in three beats: the rows that leave fade aside, the rows that stay glide to their new places and new ones rise in. As the reader scrolls, sections and entries settle from a slight backward lean; down the work log, the learning log and a case study the rail fills from Hairline to Strong Hairline as it is read and the commit being read lights its node orchid; on a case study each screen wipes in from the left and stands up as it scrolls into view. A screen opened full size grows out of its thumbnail over a fading backdrop, a step slides the next screen in from its side, and closing shrinks it back home. While a message sends, a light runs along the button's foot; field errors wipe in and each new outcome rises into the status line. On the contact page a sent message wipes in as a receipt in place of the form, its rows rising one after another, and the form wipes back in after "Write another". A copied email's check pops in. Past the hero, the status bar docks to the foot of the screen with a scroll-driven reading line. The header's orchid underline glides to the current item, and the open tab's orchid edge slides between the education and training pages. State changes are 200ms colour shifts. Reduced motion collapses all of it except what only follows the scroll (the reading line, the rail fill and the lit nodes), touch screens get the scroll depth and page turns but no tilt, and browsers without view transitions swap pages instantly. Confirmed rejections: drop shadows and glows, depth drawn with blur or bevels, rounded frames or media, hues outside the palette (technology logos excepted, as content), and code-punctuation ornaments (`#`, `@`, `<~>`) standing in for structure.
keyCharacteristics: Editor structure (explorer, tabs, status bar, file names, commit log) carries the metaphor; no glyph ornaments.
Fira Sans reads; Fira Code names files, dates, stacks, keys and status.
Three flat surface layers plus 1px hairlines; no shadows anywhere.
Square corners; full rounding only for status dots and commit nodes.
Syntax colours as roles; one filled orchid button per view.

Motion carries continuity: a gliding file highlight with a clip-path wipe, a screenshot morph into each case study, screens that grow out of their thumbnails, scroll-linked screen wipes, and rails that fill as they are read.

Depth through motion: the window opens like a lid, the window and media lean toward the mouse, a chosen screenshot turns to face the reader, blocks settle as they scroll in and pages turn like tabs; every pose eases back to flat except the project deck, the one stack that holds its depth at rest.

rules.name: The Syntax Roles Rule
rules.body: Each accent hue has one job: orchid acts and marks focus or the current item, green means live or available, amber means in progress, red means error, blue means a link leaves the text. A hue never appears outside its role.

rules.name: The One Filled Button Rule
rules.body: Only the primary action in a view gets an orchid fill. When a stronger action is present (a case study beside a live site), the other becomes a default framed button.

rules.name: The Tint, Not a New Hue Rule
rules.body: Quiet variants of an accent are the same hue at 10% fill with a 40% border (status pills). Tailwind palette colours and literal white are not part of the system; print alone is black on white (see Print).

rules.name: The Logos Are Content Rule
rules.body: Technology logos keep their brand colours, the way project screenshots and certificate images keep theirs: they are content shown at 16–20px beside a name, not UI colour, so they are the one place hues outside the palette appear, and no logo colour ever tints UI. Every logo comes through `TechIcon`, from `public/icons` where a usable file exists. A dark one-colour logo that would vanish on the canvas (Next.js, Express, Fastify, OpenAI, AWS, Prisma, shadcn/ui, CI/CD, Blueprint, T3 Stack) is redrawn in Cursor White through a CSS mask, and so is the generic API mark for REST APIs, which is not a brand. A stored file that fails at icon size is replaced by a glyph in the brand colour: MySQL's wordmark by Tabler's dolphin in MySQL blue `#4479A1`, and the solid black `drizzle.png` tile by the simple-icons mark in Drizzle lime `#C5F74F`. Technologies with no stored file use their simple-icons mark in its brand colour (Python, FastAPI, Stripe, Lemon Squeezy, discord.js); a mark whose brand colour is near-black (LangChain) or too dark to hold on the canvas (WordPress) takes Cursor White. Where no brand mark applies a generic glyph stands in, in Dim Gray, never a stand-in brand mark: a database for vector databases, a route for Mux, a document for PDF.js. A technology with nothing on file shows no logo: its name stands alone (in the about page's inventory a logo-sized gap keeps the names aligned), and in the directory's logo strip it is left out unless it is the technology being filtered on, which then shows its mono name.

rules.name: The Two Faces Rule
rules.body: Fira Sans reads; Fira Code names. File names, paths, dates, durations, stack names, keys, emails and status are mono; sentences are sans, even inside a mono list (the WhatsApp row switches to the sans because it is words, not data, and so does a language's fluency on the resume).

rules.name: The Keys Label Data Rule
rules.body: Lowercase mono keys in Soft Orchid sit directly on the data they label (definition terms, panel rows, footer columns). They are never an eyebrow above a headline; a section's file name hangs below its heading on the rule.

rules.name: The Chrome Carries the Metaphor Rule
rules.body: The editor world is expressed through structure: windows, explorers, tab strips, status bars, file tabs on rules, a commit log. Reach for one of these before any decorative device.

rules.name: The Flat Pane Rule
rules.body: No box-shadow, drop-shadow or glow on any surface, including the hero. Separation is a layer change or a 1px line.

rules.name: The Depth Is Motion Rule
rules.body: Depth is perspective, tilt and parallax that eases back to flat, never a shadow, glow, blur or bevel. A pane at rest is flat, square, 1px and shadowless; tilt is for the hero window and media only, and a rail's entries never lean one by one. The project deck is the one element that holds depth at rest: its cards stand back in real 3D, yet each stays a flat, unlit, square pane with a 1px Hairline edge, receding by tone alone.

rules.name: The Square Frame Rule
rules.body: If it has an edge, the edge is a 1px line with square corners. Roundness means "this is a status", nothing else.

dos: Do build the editor world from structure: windows, explorers, tab strips, status bars, file tabs on rules, the commit log.
Do set reading text in Fira Sans and tokens (files, dates, stacks, keys, emails, status) in Fira Code.
Do keep one orchid-filled button per view; secondary actions are default framed buttons, tertiary ones ghost.
Do separate surfaces with the three layers and 1px Hairlines; use Line Highlight for hover and selection.
Do keep each accent to its syntax role, with quiet variants as the same hue at 10% fill and 40% border.

Do use expo-out timing (`cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1)`) by default: 200ms for colour, 300ms for small transforms and rows opening in place, 420–520ms for entrances and page turns, 640ms for the screenshot turn. The exceptions: the hero lid, 1000ms on quart-out (`cubic-bezier(0.25, 1, 0.5, 1)`) so its swing is seen; a screen shrinking home, 300ms ease-in (`cubic-bezier(0.7, 0, 0.84, 0)`); filtered-out rows, gone in 120ms linear; and the sending light, a 1100ms loop on `cubic-bezier(0.65, 0, 0.35, 1)`.
